title: Undeciphered: the Phaistos Disc
summary: Found in 1908, this clay disc is now generally accepted as authentic but remains undeciphered; it is not even clear that its signs are a script. Its date is also disputed.
why: Its signs were pressed with reusable stamps, yet its message is unknown.

notes.problem: Open question had no theories (schema requires 2-4).

question: Is the stamped Phaistos Disc writing, and if so what does it say?
evidence: 45 distinct signs appear 242 times, impressed with individual stamps before firing; date estimates run from about 1850 BCE to after 1400 BCE.
wouldSettle: Another object made with the same stamps, or a longer text in the same signs.

theories.name: Greek
theories.idea: Several readings as an early Greek dialect (Hempl 1911, Faucounau, Ohlenroth and others); none accepted.

theories.name: Luwian or Anatolian
theories.idea: Achterberg and colleagues (2004) mapped its signs to Anatolian hieroglyphs and read Luwian; no reading without outside confirmation is accepted.

theories.name: Semitic
theories.idea: Aartun (1992) proposed a Semitic reading; not accepted.

theories.name: Logographic or not language
theories.idea: Haarmann (1990) read it as logographic writing; Whittaker (2005) as a votive game board.
